investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a legal actor schedule lets the origin process the new ballot and the decided advance to idx before any drain_notifiers pass observes the stale pending (the false Ok is avoided if a tick drains while decided < idx, yielding Superseded), and whether the decided entry at idx is the replacement rather than the caller's entry.

gaps.question: Is there a reachable actor schedule in which the originating node observes the new ballot and decided_idx >= assigned_idx within one drain_notifiers pass, so that the Ok arm preempts Superseded and the entry at idx is the replacement entry?

investigations.question: When a DecidedSub starts below the compacted index, does its per-element cursor arithmetic stay index-aligned with read_decided_suffix, or does it re-deliver already-emitted entries on later pushes?
investigations.hypothesis: The core returns one Trimmed/Snapshotted element in place of the whole trimmed prefix, so the vector is shorter than decided-from. push_to_sub increments next_idx once per element and push_to_all_subs assumes entries[i] is the entry at min_next+i, so after a catch-up that crosses a compaction boundary the cursor lands short of decided and later pushes re-deliver the entries after the compacted index, violating the documented in-order decided stream that applications use to apply entries once.
investigations.discriminator: The actual element count and kinds of read_decided_suffix(from) for from below versus at the compacted index on a real trimmed log, and the first later push computed from the resulting cursor.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run in which entry 5 is decided with four accepting nodes but the Decide reaches only one follower, those nodes elect a new leader whose prepare quorum excludes that follower, and the follower's late promise triggers AcceptSync: the observed decided index and the Decided/Undecided status of the same index before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

investigations.question: Does the leader's automatic trim compute the minimum accepted index over configured nodes, or do placeholder slots for absent pids force the minimum to 0 in sparse configurations?
investigations.hypothesis: LeaderState::with allocates accepted_indexes with max_pid entries initialized to 0 and indexes them by pid-1. For a configuration such as {1,2,5}, entries for pids 3 and 4 are never updated, so get_min_all_accepted_idx returns 0 even after all three configured nodes accept index 3. SequencePaxos::trim then rejects trim(Some(2)) with NotAllDecided(0) and trim(None) passes 0 to try_trim, compacting nothing, so automatic compaction never progresses.
investigations.discriminator: A three-node {1,2,5} run with three decided entries: the leader's trim(Some(2)) outcome and reported minimum, and the compacted index after trim(None), compared with the minimum accepted index over the three configured nodes.

investigations.question: Can a StopSign that a node already observed as decided become undecided again after a reconnect AcceptSync from a leader with a lower decided index, so is_reconfigured() flips Some -> None -> Some?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. stopsign_is_decided is decided_idx == accepted_idx, and is_reconfigured returns Some only while that holds. sync_log assigns the new leader's decided index unconditionally, so a node that had decided its accepted StopSign (decided == accepted) and then applies an AcceptSync carrying a lower decided index keeps the StopSign accepted but no longer decided. is_reconfigured therefore returns None until the new leader re-decides the StopSign, after which it returns Some again.

history.question: Can a follower that promised a stable leader but missed the AcceptStopSign recover after that StopSign becomes decided, or is it stuck behind with decided < accepted-by-others and no enabled repair?
history.hypothesis: It is stuck. resend_messages_leader resends the StopSign Decide once stopsign_is_decided and resends AcceptStopSign only while the StopSign is undecided. send_decide resends with the last used sequence number, and even an accepted Decide cannot advance a follower whose accepted index is below the decision: update_decided_idx_and_get_accepted_idx clamps decided to the flushed accepted index, so the follower stays at its old decided value. AcceptSync, which would carry the missing StopSign and the leader's decided index, is sent only in response to a Promise, and a stable leader sends Prepare only to peers that are not promised. The follower therefore makes no progress until leadership changes or the user reconnects it.

investigations.question: Can append_notify resolve Ok(idx) for an entry that lost leadership before decision and was replaced at idx by a different decided entry?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes: Pending keeps only (assigned_idx, ballot_at_assignment). drain_notifiers first resolves Ok whenever idx <= decided, before the ballot < cur_ballot arm, and never reads the log to compare the decided value at idx with the pending entry. When the originating node's locally accepted entry is overwritten by a new leader and the replacement at idx is decided, the origin's decided_idx advances to idx while the pending ballot is stale, so Ok(idx) reports completion of an entry that was never decided.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.
